solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Songs to entertain bishop in ecclesiastical grounds

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the songs enclose the bishop

parts.note: glees are part-songs for unaccompanied voices
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Choristers singing to a visiting bishop out in the cathedral close.
explanation.definitionFit: A glebe is a piece of land attached to a parish benefice, providing income for the clergy.

clue.text: Plan to have second person in apartment when the first has gone

indicators.note: in places the second person inside the shortened apartment
the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
you is the second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone plans to move a second lodger in once the first tenant has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when the first has gone' leaves LAT; 'in' then puts the pronoun inside. 'Plan' and 'apartment' together suggest housing, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout is the arrangement or design of something, a plan of how it fits together.

clue.text: Having a go at living without politicians

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the living wraps the politicians

parts.note: being means existing, living
Labour, the British political party

explanation.surface: Trying to live with no politicians at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking'; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Belabouring someone is attacking them, verbally or physically; having a go at is the British idiom for that.

clue.text: One legally controlled by a couple of letters?

definitions.text: One legally controlled by a couple of letters?

parts.words: One legally controlled by a couple of letters?
parts.note: letters here are people who let property; someone renting from a tenant is under two landlords in turn

explanation.surface: Someone whose legal fate rests on just two characters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: This occupant rents from a tenant, so is bound by both that tenant and the owner above.

clue.text: Demonstrated in front of church somewhere in France

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the second in the answer

parts.note: something demonstrated has been shown to be true, i.e. proven
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone has proved their worth ahead of a church service in rural France.
explanation.definitionFit: Provence is a region in the south-east of France, so it is literally a place there.

clue.text: Walking in a particular direction, overtake worker?

parts.note: to pass another vehicle is to overtake it
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A walker overtakes a labourer going the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, an animal shown walking with one forepaw raised, facing left, is described with this term.

clue.text: Finished on time and open to view

parts.note: over means finished

explanation.surface: Work done on schedule and on display for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden or secret.

clue.text: English army officer can be a pig

parts.note: LT is short for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A boorish English officer behaving like a swine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pig' looks like an insult for the officer; it is a farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An elt is a dialect word for a young sow, a crossword regular.

clue.text: More cheerful right after cooking rich food

indicators.note: after puts right at the end, following the other pieces
cooking suggests ingredients mixed up, so the letters of rich are rearranged

parts.note: a pie is a kind of food

explanation.surface: A diner perks up after eating a rich dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chirpy means lively and cheerful, and the comparative means more so.

clue.text: Course is creamy dessert with new finishing touch

indicators.note: the finishing touch is the final letter, which is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a syllabub is a whipped cream dessert flavoured with wine or sherry

explanation.surface: A dessert course gets a fresh garnish at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The last B of SYLLABUB is changed to S; the clue does not say which letter comes in, so the definition settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of a course of study, so it can stand for the course itself.

clue.text: Need to take sick to one part of hospital

indicators.note: to here means attached to, so the ailing comes joined after the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
to ail is to be or fall ill

explanation.surface: A patient needs to be taken to a hospital ward after falling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to involve it necessarily, so it is a verb synonym for require or need.

clue.text: Cross about doctor's indistinct utterance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cross is placed around the doctor

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An irritated patient complains about the doctor's unclear speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry; it is the noun, a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mumble is speech spoken too quietly or unclearly to be heard properly.

clue.text: Dad in a new relationship, a man challenging religious authority

indicators.note: in places the father inside the other letters

parts.note: a tie is a bond or connection between people
pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father starts a new romance, while some rebel defies the church.
explanation.definitionFit: An antipope is a rival claimant to the papacy, set up in opposition to the recognised Pope.

clue.text: Assiduous old man in street meeting a top man

parts.note: pa, informal for father
a king is the man at the very top

explanation.surface: A diligent father out on the street meets the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Assiduous and painstaking both describe careful, thorough effort.

clue.text: A foreign writer is confronting text-changer lacking official status

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so the word is sits right up against the editor

parts.note: un is French for a
an author is a writer
ED is short for editor, who changes a writer's text

explanation.surface: A writer from abroad faces down an editor, but has no official standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without authorisation lacks the formal permission or status that would make it legitimate.

clue.text: A bit set on changing — or maybe not!

definitions.text: A bit set on changing — or maybe not!

indicators.note: changing says these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is slightly keen on change, then suddenly refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue describes someone who will not change: that is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person refuses to change their mind or behaviour.

clue.text: Hero, number one cricketer coming in for a drink

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the pieces go inside the hero

parts.note: a lion is a hero, a celebrated brave person
I is the Roman numeral one
a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: The star batsman comes in to bat and is rewarded with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is a drink poured as an offering, or jokingly any alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Don't expect any of them to give you the bigger picture

definitions.text: Don't expect any of them to give you the bigger picture

parts.words: Don't expect any of them to give you the bigger picture
parts.note: an idiom for an overview, taken literally: these artists paint only very small portraits and scenes

explanation.surface: A warning that some people can never see the overall situation.
explanation.definitionFit: These painters specialise in tiny works, so a big picture is the last thing they produce.

clue.text: Cut grass covering bird, except for tail

indicators.note: covering puts the grass around the shortened bird

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a duck is a bird

explanation.surface: Mowing reeds that shelter a bird, sparing only its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for tail' leaves DUC; 'covering' wraps the grass around it. 'Cut' reads as a verb but works as the adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced as an adjective means lowered or cut, as in reduced prices.

clue.text: Prince and king entertained by favourite after game

indicators.note: after places the remaining piece behind the game

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside the favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Royals and a favourite guest enjoying themselves after a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Rupert of the Rhine was a Royalist cavalry commander in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Aimed to purchase, breaking into new trade

indicators.note: breaking into says one piece forces its way inside the other
new signals that the letters of trade are put in a fresh order

parts.note: to get something can mean to buy it

explanation.surface: A business set out to buy its way into a fresh market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives TARED; 'breaking into' sets the purchase inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Targeted means directed at a goal, a close synonym of aimed.

clue.text: First Oscar is too much for opera singer

indicators.note: is too much for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Winning an Oscar first time is overwhelming for a diva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Oscar' holds one letter too many at each end: drop the F, I, R, S and the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Floria Tosca is the soprano heroine of Puccini's opera, herself an opera singer.

clue.text: Minister losing head going to America, one on hazardous trip

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a vicar is a minister of the church
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A priest heads off to the States on a risky journey.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell, the most perilous of flights.

clue.text: Several people looking for shipwreck?

definitions.meaning: an old word meaning sundry or various

explanation.surface: Several people hunting for a sunken ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers as an adjective means various; as a plural noun it means underwater swimmers.

clue.text: Female bad, not half, ending in shame

indicators.note: not half means only half the word is kept

parts.note: evil means bad

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A woman behaving badly, though only half so, ends up in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, whose name stands for any woman.

clue.text: Church woman beginning to shine vessels there

parts.note: Alice is a woman's name

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A churchwoman starts polishing the vessels kept there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' refers back to the church: these are vessels found in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalices are the goblets used to hold wine at Communion in a church.

clue.text: Certainly, cutting energy used around island is sought after

indicators.note: used around means placed surrounding, so the shortened word wraps the island
cutting here means removing a letter from the word

parts.note: indeed means certainly
E is the physics symbol for energy
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An energy-saving island project is said to be highly popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' leaves INDED; 'used around' wraps that round the island, the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wanted by many people is popular, a direct synonym of sought after.

clue.text: Significant wicket falling — score short of a hundred

indicators.note: a falling wicket is lost, so that letter drops out

parts.note: weighty means important or significant
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: a key wicket falls with the team short of a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and one score below a hundred is the number eighty.
